children: The Government of Singapore receives 17.79 lakh shares, accounting for 16.8 per cent of the total shares allotted under the QIP

Shares of Bharat Forge will be in focus on Wednesday after the auto components maker raised Rs 2,000 crore through a qualified institutional placement (QIP), with the Government of Singapore emerging as the largest allottee.

The company’s investment committee approved the allotment of 1.05 crore equity shares to eligible qualified institutional buyers at an issue price of Rs 1,890 per share, Bharat Forge said in an exchange filing on Tuesday. The issue price represents a 5.5 per cent discount to the stock’s closing price of Rs 2,001.40 on Tuesday.

The Government of Singapore received 17.79 lakh shares, accounting for 16.8 per cent of the total shares allotted under the QIP. ICICI Prudential Large and Mid Cap Fund, ICICI Prudential Multi Cap Fund and ISIF Active Asset Allocator Long-Short Fund were each allotted 10.58 lakh shares, or around 10 per cent of the issue.
Two custodian mutual funds of Invesco India received a combined 7.4 lakh shares, representing around 7 per cent of the shares issued through the QIP.

Following the allotment, Bharat Forge’s subscribed and fully paid-up equity share capital increased to Rs 977 crore from Rs 956 crore. The company’s outstanding equity shares have risen to around 488.5 crore from 478 crore, with each share having a face value of Rs 2.

Bharat Forge launched the QIP on September 17 with a floor price of Rs 1,851 per share. The final issue price of Rs 1,890 was therefore set above the floor price, although at a discount to the prevailing market price.

The fund-raising comes as Bharat Forge continues to expand its presence across automotive and industrial applications. The company has been among the major Indian auto component manufacturers, with operations spanning forged and machined components and other engineering products.
The fresh equity issued through the QIP will increase the company’s share count and broaden its institutional shareholder base following the fund-raise.
